property_tests.description: For any spec with N correctness_properties and M property_tests, ValidateCrossFile returns exactly one integrity error per property whose property_id does not appear in any property_test.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate specs with 0-10 correctness_properties (random IDs) and 0-10 property_tests (random property_id values drawn from a mix of the property IDs and unrelated IDs); enumerate all uncovered property IDs (those not referenced by any property_test).
property_tests.invariant_check: uncovered = {p.id for p in spec.correctness_properties} - {pt.property_id for pt in spec.test_spec.property_tests}; entries = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); prop_errors = [e for e in entries if e.Category == 'integrity' and e.RequirementID in uncovered]; assert len(prop_errors) == len(uncovered); assert all(e.RequirementID in uncovered for e in prop_errors)

property_tests.description: For any spec with N execution_paths and M smoke_tests, ValidateCrossFile returns exactly one integrity error per execution_path whose execution_path_id does not appear in any smoke_test.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate specs with 0-10 execution_paths (random IDs) and 0-10 smoke_tests (random execution_path_id values drawn from a mix of the path IDs and unrelated IDs); enumerate all uncovered path IDs.
property_tests.invariant_check: uncovered = {p.id for p in spec.execution_paths} - {st.execution_path_id for st in spec.test_spec.smoke_tests}; entries = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); path_errors = [e for e in entries if e.Category == 'integrity' and any(uid in e.Message for uid in uncovered)]; assert len(path_errors) == len(uncovered)

property_tests.description: For any backtick-wrapped term extracted from a criterion or property field, the term is excluded from glossary checks if and only if it is numeric, a single character, a quoted string, or longer than 80 characters.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate terms from four categories: (a) numeric strings including negatives and decimals, (b) single-character strings, (c) strings wrapped in single or double quotes, (d) strings of length 81+, (e) normal multi-character non-numeric strings of length 2-80; embed each as a backtick term in a criterion action field; use an empty glossary.
property_tests.invariant_check: for each term in categories (a)-(d): entries = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); assert no entry has term in its Message; for each term in category (e): assert exactly one entry has term in its Message and Category == 'integrity'

property_tests.description: For any spec with any number of traceability entries, ValidateCrossFile returns exactly N-1 errors for any (requirement_id, test_spec_id) pair appearing N times (N>1), and zero errors for pairs appearing exactly once.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate traceability entry lists where each (requirement_id, test_spec_id) pair appears between 1 and 5 times; use random requirement_id and test_spec_id strings; track expected duplicate counts per pair.
property_tests.invariant_check: from collections import Counter; pair_counts = Counter((e.requirement_id, e.test_spec_id) for e in spec.traceability); entries = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); dup_errors = [e for e in entries if e.Category == 'integrity' and 'duplicate' in e.Message.lower()]; expected_total = sum(max(0, c-1) for c in pair_counts.values()); assert len(dup_errors) == expected_total

property_tests.description: For any spec, the 'valid' field in ValidateStructured output is true if and only if the 'errors' slice is empty.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate specs ranging from fully valid (no violations) to specs with 1-5 injected violations (missing property tests, duplicate traceability, unwanted criteria without return_contract); call ValidateStructured on each.
property_tests.invariant_check: output = spec.ValidateStructured(); assert output['valid'] == (len(output['errors']) == 0); assert type(output['valid']) == bool

property_tests.description: Warning rules for group test_spec_refs (>15), group subtask count (>6), and subtask test_spec_refs (>8) produce no warning at exactly the threshold value and exactly one warning at threshold+1.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: For each of the three warning rules, generate specs at exactly the threshold value and at threshold+1; use random but valid subtask and test_spec_refs content to fill counts.
property_tests.invariant_check: // Group refs ceiling: spec_at_15 = spec with group total refs == 15; result = spec_at_15.Validate(); assert no ceiling warning; spec_at_16 = spec with group total refs == 16; result = spec_at_16.Validate(); assert exactly one ceiling warning; // Group subtask count: spec_at_6 = spec with 6 non-verification subtasks; assert no count warning; spec_at_7 = spec with 7; assert exactly one count warning; // Subtask refs ceiling: spec_at_8 = spec with subtask having 8 refs; assert no warning; spec_at_9 = spec with 9 refs; assert exactly one warning

property_tests.description: ValidateCrossFile returns exactly one integrity error for each criterion with ears_pattern='unwanted' and a null or empty return_contract, and zero errors for unwanted criteria with a non-empty return_contract.
property_tests.for_any_strategy: Generate specs with 0-10 criteria having ears_pattern='unwanted'; randomly assign return_contract as null, empty string, or a non-empty string; track which criteria should produce errors.
property_tests.invariant_check: missing = [c for c in all_criteria if c.ears_pattern == 'unwanted' and (c.return_contract is null or c.return_contract == '')]; entries = spec.ValidateCrossFile(); unwanted_errors = [e for e in entries if e.Category == 'integrity' and any(c.id in e.Message for c in missing)]; assert len(unwanted_errors) == len(missing); covered = [c for c in all_criteria if c.ears_pattern == 'unwanted' and c.return_contract not in [null, '']]; covered_errors = [e for e in entries if any(c.id in e.Message for c in covered)]; assert len(covered_errors) == 0

smoke_tests.description: Full cross-file validation run on a spec that violates all 7 cross-file rules returns a combined ValidationEntry slice with errors from each rule.
smoke_tests.trigger: Call spec.ValidateCrossFile() on a *Spec constructed to violate all 7 cross-file rules simultaneously: missing property_test coverage, missing smoke_test coverage, unresolvable test_spec_ids, undefined backtick terms, duplicate traceability pairs, unresolvable requirement_refs, and unwanted criteria without return_contract.
expected_effects: Returns a []ValidationEntry with at least 7 entries (one per violated rule)
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and RequirementID referencing the uncovered correctness_property
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and Message referencing the uncovered execution_path_id
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and Message referencing the unresolvable test_spec_id
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and Message referencing the undefined backtick term
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and Message referencing the duplicate traceability pair
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and Message referencing the unresolvable requirement_ref
Contains at least one entry with Category='integrity' and Message referencing the unwanted criterion missing return_contract
Does not panic; returns cleanly to the caller

smoke_tests.description: ValidateStructured call on a spec with errors and warnings produces a structured map with correct keys, field shapes, and valid=false.
smoke_tests.trigger: Call spec.ValidateStructured() on a *Spec that has at least one integrity error (missing property test) and at least one warning (more than 10 requirements).
expected_effects: Returns a non-nil map[string]any
Map contains key 'valid' with value false (bool)
Map contains key 'errors' with a non-empty slice of map[string]any
Each error map contains keys: 'category', 'rule', 'message', 'file', 'path' — all non-empty strings
Integrity errors have category='integrity'
Map contains key 'warnings' with a non-empty slice of map[string]any
Each warning map contains keys: 'message' and 'entity_id'
Does not panic or return nil

smoke_tests.description: Cross-spec validation run detects API symbol signature mismatch and unknown dependency reference, returning combined integrity errors.
smoke_tests.trigger: Call ValidateCrossSpec(specs, graph) where specs contains specA (declaring symbol 'Foo' with signature 'func Foo() int' and a task dependency depends_on_spec='specZ') and specB (declaring 'Foo' with signature 'func Foo() string'), and graph has an edge specA -> specB; 'specZ' is not in the spec map.
expected_effects: Returns a []ValidationEntry with at least two entries
Contains one entry with Category='integrity' identifying 'Foo' signature mismatch between specA and specB
Contains one entry with Category='integrity' identifying 'specZ' as an unknown depends_on_spec reference
Does not panic; returns cleanly to the caller

smoke_tests.description: Full Validate run on a large spec with vague language and oversized groups produces a ValidationResult with warnings and correct Valid flag.
smoke_tests.trigger: Call spec.Validate() on a *Spec with 11 requirements, one task group containing 7 non-verification subtasks, and a criterion whose action field contains the word 'appropriately'.
expected_effects: Returns a ValidationResult struct
ValidationResult.Warnings contains at least three entries: one for scope limit (more than 10 requirements), one for group subtask count (more than 6), one for vague language ('appropriately')
ValidationResult.Valid is true if Errors is empty, false otherwise
ValidationResult.Errors contains only schema or integrity entries (no warnings mixed in)
Does not panic; returns cleanly to the caller
